processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Five Cu molds were moved stepwise inside the furnace and successively filled with melt from a 4-kg ingot; after each cast the remaining melt composition was adjusted by charging Al through an air lock.

processing_steps.reduction_ratio: from 10 × 50 × 130 mm³ blocks to 2 ± 0.1 mm thick and ~500 mm long sheets

processing_steps.method: cutting perpendicular to rolling direction into segments
processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Segments of dimensions 2 × 60 × 55 mm³ for each alloy composition.
Aging conducted at 450, 500, 550, and 600 °C for 0 h, 1 h, and 24 h; this sample corresponds to 500 °C / 1 h.
Scales were removed from the surfaces after the heat treatments.
Samples for mechanical testing and microstructure investigation were prepared from the segments by package spark erosion.

structures.overall_structure: Fully recrystallized austenitic microstructure with nm-sized κ-carbide precipitates formed during aging at 500 °C for 1 h

precipitates.distribution: formed during aging at 500 °C for 1 h

interfaces.phase_evolution: nm-sized κ-carbides form during aging at 500 °C for 1 h
interfaces.interface_notes: κ-carbides have ordered fcc (L'1₂) structure; lattice mismatch <3% with austenitic Fe-Mn-C matrix enables cuboidal nanoprecipitates; in a ferritic matrix the mismatch can be as large as -6%, giving semicoherent interfaces.

measurement_conditions.other_conditions: All plotted values represent averages of three measurements for every material state.

characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: room temperature; initial strain rate 10^-3 s^-1
characterization_methods.purpose: mechanical screening (yield strength, ultimate tensile strength, total elongation)
characterization_methods.key_findings: Aging for 1 h increases YS, UTS, and hardness and only minorly reduces TE for Fe-30Mn-1.2C-8Al.
Hardness increases with aging; Figure 3d shows hardness rises steeply at 8Al toward ~375 HBW (highest curve corresponding to 550 °C/24 h).

characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: performed on the rolling plane of samples ground to a thickness of 1 mm
cross-sectional areas prepared in the plane perpendicular to the rolling direction
characterization_methods.purpose: inspection for cracks, pores, or macrosegregations
characterization_methods.key_findings: no cracks, pores, or macrosegregations in the final materials

unmapped_findings: For Fe-30Mn-1.2C-8Al (this sample's alloy), aging for 1 h — including the 500 °C/1 h condition — leads to an increase in YS, UTS, and hardness (increasing with temperature) and only a minor reduction in TE; aging for 24 h further raises YS, UTS, and hardness to levels twice as high as the as-homogenized state and drastically reduces ductility (b0024). Exact numeric YS/UTS/TE/hardness for the 500 °C/1 h condition are not tabulated in the text.
The pronounced strengthening of the ~8 wt.% Al variant during aging is attributed to the formation of nm-sized κ-carbides (b0025).
After aging at 500–600 °C, mechanical twinning is reduced and strain hardening is essentially associated with κ-carbide and solid-solution strengthening (b0031).

Proposed deformation mechanism for κ-carbide-strengthened austenitic steels: Orowan bypassing of longitudinal κ-carbide rods, subsequent expansion of dislocation loops assisted by dislocation cross-slip, and (to a minor extent) shearing of κ-carbides; higher dislocation densities in dislocation bundles are attributed to minor spacing differences between κ-carbide rods (b0032, b0035). This mechanism is described for regularly arranged nanosized κ-carbides such as those in the 600 °C/24 h sample (Fig. 5), not directly measured on the 500 °C/1 h sample.

In Fig. 4, the 8Al (this alloy) purple series reaches the highest tensile strength (~800–950 MPa) among the Fe-30Mn-1.2C-xAl alloys; the exact 500 °C/1 h point is not separately tabulated (figure_004).

In Fig. 3, the 500 °C/1 h condition is plotted as the red curve; at 8Al the extreme values visible in the figure (YS ~900 MPa, UTS ~1000 MPa, hardness ~375 HBW, TE ~10%) correspond to the 550 °C/24 h or 24 h conditions, so no exact 500 °C/1 h value could be extracted for this sample (figure_003).
